## Preface to the Reader.

It is a common proverb, used as much among the Latins as among us Germans, which says: *Art has no enemy except the ignorant* <note>original Latin: "Ars non habet inimicum, nisi ignorantem"</note>. This means that Art has no greater enemy than the one who does not know or understand it. And although this can be said **generally** of every art, it is nonetheless **specifically** and primarily to be said—and lamented—regarding the noble, secret, indeed rather heavenly art of <term>Alchemy</term> <note>The original uses the term *Chymia*. In this period, the term spanned the spectrum from practical laboratory chemistry to the spiritual and transformative work of alchemy.</note>, that it is despised, nullified, belittled, and slandered by almost everyone as a

# Preface.

Since, then, without doubt, many people are by nature inclined and prone to such **Philosophy**: and would gladly practice and utilize it, if only they had good instruction for it; and since recently the *Philosophical Compendium* <note>original: *Compendium Philosophicum*; a concise handbook or summary of philosophical and alchemical knowledge.</note> of Master <note>original: *Domini*.</note> **Michael Potier of Étain** <note>A French alchemist active in the early 17th century, known for his travels and works on the transmutation of metals.</note> was given to me by the author himself, and I noticed that through this work a fine report and sufficient instruction could be given to many: I have therefore had it printed alongside the three aforementioned small treatises. <note>original: *tractätlein*; refers to the specific collection of essays or pamphlets contained in this volume.</note> I would therefore kindly ask the gracious reader to favorably accept this diligent effort.

# The Sixteenth Experiment

# The second degree follows, by which the water is also increased, through fixed Mercury.

Seal it well with luting and **distill** <term>distill <note>To purify a liquid by heating it into vapor and then condensing it back into liquid form.</note></term> it as before; in this way, the Mercury will sublimate upwards...

# Preface

...informed, you should first highly exercise yourself in **Theory** or **Speculation**, as well as in **Practice**, and test your opinion with certain causes or **Reasons** <note>original: "Rationibus"</note>, likewise with true experience.

<margin>Sophistical</margin>
Secondly, you should avoid "philosophical" books <note>In this context, "philosophical" refers to alchemical texts written by the "philosophers" or adepts of the art.</note> and their **Recipes**. # Preface

Take it for certain that no **physician** <note>original: "Medicus"</note> can be sure of his art unless he diligently devotes himself to this Art [Alchemy], because all **distillation**, **preparation** of medicine, and other secret **philosophical techniques** <note>original: "Philosophische Griffe"; referring to the specialized laboratory maneuvers and chemical manipulations used by alchemists to extract essences.</note>—which in this case can help nature more than herbs, and are hidden within metals—depend on this Art alone. # Bernard

...earnestness, and for so long a time, and similarly pursued with such great expense; yet one is unwilling to spend even six or seven months on this Art, whereas one follows and pursues other trivial trades for twice as many years.

Since it is such a noble and exceedingly rich Art, it is not fitting to reveal <note>original: "reueliren"</note> it to the unworthy. Yet I tell you: whomever God opens the eyes so that he might attain it and finally grasp it, that person will be ashamed of the **detours** <term>Detours: original "Vmbschweiff," referring to the convoluted and unnecessary chemical procedures many alchemists performed before discovering the "simple" or "natural" way.</term> he took within it; for it is so easy and well-performed that, if I were to show it to you, you would hardly believe this simple path. 

For this reason, all who possessed it have hidden such Art with words and described <note>original: "describiert"</note> and indicated it in such a strange manner. They were always concerned that one might understand it too quickly; therefore, their books are so difficult to understand for those who have not attained the foundation <note>original: "grund"</note>. For apart from the **transformation of nature** <note>original: "naturæ mutationē"</note>, it is impossible for them to bring the secrets of the Philosophers to a perfect end <note>original: "perfectum finem"</note>.

# First Part.

I vi

Note all that Hermes says here in this book. Although it is short, these are nonetheless great words, and the entire <term>Art</term> <note>The "Art" of Alchemy, or the Hermetic tradition of transformation</note> and the whole <term>Work</term> <note>original: "Werck"; the Great Work or *Magnum Opus* aimed at creating the Philosopher's Stone</note> are properly described within it. Afterwards, following Hermes, Pythagoras truly possessed it; he was Hermes's disciple, who produced the *Assembly of the Philosophers* <note>original Latin: *Turbam Philosophorum*; one of the oldest and most influential alchemical texts in the West, written as a record of a meeting of various sages</note>, which is called by some the *Codex of Truth* <note>original Latin: *Codex veritatis*</note>, and not without reason, for the pure truth is found within it. Although there are now many who are named in it and are partly incomprehensible to the reader, Pythagoras nonetheless composed and wrote it himself in this manner with all diligence and not without cause. Furthermore, it was possessed by Bendigud Jesu <note>A name often found in medieval alchemical lineages, possibly a corrupted reference to an Arabic or Syriac authority such as Apollonius of Tyana</note>, Aristotle, and Alexander—a king in Macedonia and a disciple of Aristotle. they were to be united: <note>original Latin: "Etsi esset commiscibilis eorum perfectio cum imperfectis, non imperfecta cum perfectis perficerentur, sed eorum perfectio cum imperfectis diminueretur."</note> **"Even if their perfection could be mixed with the imperfect, the imperfect would not be perfected by the perfect; rather, the perfection of the perfect would be diminished by the imperfect."**

When **heat** works upon **moisture**, you will first see a **black color** <note>This describes *Nigredo*, the initial "blackening" or putrefaction stage of the alchemical process, where the material is broken down.</note>. For into whatever substance a thing has its origin, it is most possible for it to return to that same substance.

# ALANI
<note>Likely referring to Alanus ab Insulis (Alain de Lille), a 12th-century theologian and poet to whom various alchemical treatises were later attributed.</note>

# Of the Great Stone

...right <note>completing the thought from the previous page: a "matter which is right"</note> [and] can have no other [name] than the **Great Stone of the World**, which penetrates human and metallic bodies like a spirit. It is a **universal medicine** <note>original: *vniuersal Medicin*; a panacea capable of curing all diseases and perfecting "base" metals into gold</note> without defect, for it drives out the evil and preserves the good. It is also a perfection, such that the evil must be turned into good at the same time. Its color ranges from a transparent redness to a dark brown, from a **ruby-color** to that of **garnets**, and in weight, it is mighty and exceedingly heavy.

Whoever obtains such a Stone should thank the highest **Creator** of all creatures for such a **Heavenly Balsam**, and pray for himself and his neighbor that he may use the same for the temporal maintenance of this **vale of tears** <note>original: *Jammerthal*; a common historical and religious metaphor for the suffering and trials of earthly life</note>, and in the world to come, that he may afterwards have eternal **welfare**. May God be highly praised in eternity for His unspeakable gift and grace.

## The Eleventh Key.

I will present and make known to you the **eleventh key** of the **multiplication** <note>original: *Vermehrung*; in alchemy, this is the process of increasing the quantity or the transformative power of the Philosopher's Stone</note> of our **Great Stone** by means of a parable.

There lived in the **Orient** <note>original: *Morgenlande*; literally "morning-land," referring to the East. In alchemy, the East often symbolizes the beginning of the work or the rising of spiritual light</note> a noble knight named **Orpheus**, who was exceedingly rich in goods and very mighty in all his means. He had chosen his own biological and natural sister, named **Euridice**, for marriage, recognizing and taking her as his wife. However, because he could obtain no heirs with her, and attributed the cause to the sin of having chosen his sister as a wife, he constantly petitioned the **Most High** <note>referring to God</note> with diligent persistence, praying that He might bestow a blessing upon him and grant the fulfillment of his request.
